CURRENT EVALUATION STATUS — corrected 2026-11-15 against Greg's later decisions recorded in rules-greg-evaluation-on-engram-2026-11-09, rules-greg-evaluation-on-termal-2026-11-10 and rules-authority-and-landing. Independent acceptance evaluation is ON for Engram (since 2026-11-09 07:07:38Z) and TermAl (since 2026-11-10 19:43:17Z). Engram::Asistant relayed Greg's words for Engram in mailbox 43498a6e #748: „Wlącz dla Engram.” For TermAl, #868/message eaf73641: „mysle, ze mozemy wlaczyc Ewaluacje dla Termal, to nasz nastepny etap testow”. This is a correction of stale attributed guidance, not a policy change or new authority. Completion needs the independent evaluation the current repository and project policy require; a missing verdict stays pending and never becomes a forged pass. Broken mechanisms are reported and repaired while authorized independent work continues.

HISTORICAL GREG WORD, superseded for evaluation in these two projects: the 2026-11-02 acting conversation with Engram::Architect3 recorded:
"Engram::Fable sie zatkal czekajac ma moj input
TO NIE JEST ACEPTOWALNE

independent acceptance evaluation first,
THIS SHIT IS TURNED OFF
UNTIL WE GOT THIS WORKING"
That temporary evaluation-OFF direction and its self-asserted-completion route no longer apply to Engram or TermAl after the later explicit reactivations above. The simple-procedure guidance below remains subject to current criteria, bindings, required reviews, independent evaluation and repository authority. Evaluation and turn gating are distinct; this correction changes neither policy nor live authority.

TEMPORARY SIMPLE PROCEDURE — until the procedural mechanisms are repaired. Greg direct to Engram::Architect3: "prosze o uproszczone procedury do czasu naprawiania bledow proceduralnych". This is the single current operating text; incident history and earlier interpretations stay in task notes.

1. CODER: implement the fix, run the focused checks and obtain the reviews the repository requires. Send the Merger ONE complete READY with the exact input, result references and resolved findings. Intermediate progress stays on the task or with the coordinator.
2. MERGER: integrate, run the required validation on the exact final input, then land under existing standing approval or the acting session's direct permission. Reuse valid existing evidence where the current rules allow it. No extra review, repeated successful test or repeated routine 'go' for paperwork alone.
3. BROKEN PROCEDURE: if evaluation, observation, credit or settlement fails because its mechanism is broken, record ONCE on the item: actual input/build and result references, exact missing/refused step and its defect owner. Continue authorized repairs and independent work. An unobtained evaluation remains pending; never invent a pass, native credit or completed seal. Use an existing supported exception already authorized for that executor when applicable.
4. RUNS AND COMMUNICATION: TermAl runs, stores logs and wakes the responsible owner; agents read terminal metadata and bounded failure diagnostics. No stdout following, polling, duplicate evidence bundles/manual hash manifests for native records, extra checklists, approval rounds or per-step compliance acknowledgements. Report a result, a real blocker or a collaboration defect, not routine partial status. Return to each repaired mechanism when available. The coordinator consolidates repeated status and preservation questions from existing evidence; interrupt a critical repair's coder only for new facts or decisions needed to implement or validate that repair.

Technical failures still need repair and a failed test is not a pass. Claims, store integrity, repository landing conditions, executor-scoped permissions and Greg's TermAl restart remain governed by their actual instructions; the temporary procedure adds no new permission barrier or authority.

SOURCES: the text above relayed verbatim by Engram::Architect3 (#173, message 7a46bee4-a324-4f92-a6e7-2ab7e439e392, 2026-10-30T19:55:09Z) from Greg's direct request in its acting chat. Related earlier Greg word, relayed by Engram::Advisor #2377 (message 300499d9, 19:50:00Z): „prosze zespol o zdrowy rozsadek.. jak test przejdzie i jest OK prosze o pominiecie precedur, do czasu naprawienia mechanizmow. TO NIE MOZE BYC BLOCKEREM teraz”.

ADMISSION/SETTLEMENT INCIDENTS: separate the known failure cause from an unknown prior operation outcome. A generic degraded/unknown code is not a sufficient incident report: retain the concrete persistence/transport error, affected and causal session/operation scope, current boundary, and the responsible recovery owner/next supported action. Preserve the original intent/key and queued user content; never clear the hold, cancel user work or create new authority merely to make status green. Apply existing STOP/rollback rules through the authorized actor when their actual conditions hold; OFF does not settle old authority. If Advisor is blocked, the coordinator reports directly through an available channel. Correct the existing mechanism; no repeated blind Resume or duplicate run, new checklist/approval gate or readiness claim before actual recovery.

GREG DIRECT, 2026-11-01: "NIE CHCE HOT FIX"; "jest zawodny"; user prompts were supposed to be outside gated control. Repair the end-to-end existing mechanism; do not ship a symptom-only exclusion bypass. Explicit human prompts do not require gated Evaluate/Begin/grant and must not be stranded behind stale control settlement. Preserve/reconcile original authority and queued content separately, without duplicate provider effects or new tool permissions. Existing coders/coordinators own the coherent repair and actual recovery proof. The earlier Central persistence failure and restart restrictions are incident history, not a current runtime observation; current restart readiness follows actual coordinator/build/store evidence. No re-enable from old approval or unsupported ETA.
